title: 'Dopamine Sites' Let You Shop Without Spending Money
paragraphs: Have you ever filled an online shopping cart, looked at the total — and then closed the website without buying anything?
A new internet trend takes that idea even further. So-called "dopamine sites" let people shop, order food and even plan holidays without paying anything — because none of it is real.

The trend started in South Korea in spring 2026 and quickly became popular, especially among young people looking for entertainment or comfort without spending money. It has since spread to other countries.

Some sites look just like food ordering apps. You can choose dishes, add extras, place an "order" and even watch the food make its way to you on the screen — but no money is spent and no food ever arrives. One example is FoodNeverComes.com, created by two software developers in India, which has had more than 2.7 million visitors since it went online in June.

Others work like online stores. Dopamine Shop, for example, lets users fill their carts with expensive clothes, jewelry and other items, and "order" them without actually buying — or paying for — anything.
So why can buying nothing still feel good?
Experts say part of what makes shopping enjoyable happens before we get anything. Looking at items, choosing the ones we want and looking forward to getting them can all feel good on their own.

Some users also say dopamine sites help them resist impulse buying or food orders they don't really need. However, experts say it's still too early to know whether dopamine sites can help people change their real spending habits in the long term.

The sites could also just look exciting because they're new, and people may get bored with them over time. Still, their popularity so far shows that for many people, shopping is fun — even without buying anything!
